sections.heading: The dashboard
sections.markdown:
`/sessions` is where you run and watch coding agents. The sidebar on the left lists every live session as a card, grouped by repo, and the session area on the right shows the selected session's terminal. You type into that terminal as you would in your own.

A session is either an agent (Claude, Codex or pi) working on a prompt or an assist command such as `/draft`, or a **run** session that executes one of the repo's `run` entries, such as a dev server.

{{screenshot:sessions-dashboard.png}}

Here the sandbox repo has three sessions, so they share a group: an agent waiting on an answer, a dev server and an agent still working. The `api` and `website` repos have one session each, so their cards stand alone.

screenshots.alt: The sessions dashboard with agents in three repos and a dev server

sections.heading: Starting it
sections.markdown:
```bash
assist
```

`assist` with no arguments, `assist sessions` and `assist sessions web` all start the web server on port 3100 and open it in your browser. `assist sessions web --port <n>` picks another port, and `--no-open` skips the browser.

sections.heading: The toolbar
sections.markdown:
From left to right:

- **Refresh** restarts the web server. Sessions keep running.
- **Tabs**: Sessions, Backlog and Next, plus Releases when the selected repo has releases configured and News when you have feeds. Alt+1 to Alt+5 switch between them.
- **Repo picker** chooses the repo the toolbar acts on. It lists the repo the web server started in plus every repo a session has run in; type to filter. Selecting a card switches it to that card's repo.
- **VS Code** opens the selected repo in VS Code, and **GitHub** opens it on GitHub.
- **+** opens the new-session dialog (see [Creating sessions](../sessions-creating/)).
- A **PRs** menu appears when the repo has open pull requests, and a run menu when the repo has `run` entries.
- **Usage** opens `/usage`. Once rate-limit data arrives it shows your current limits instead.
- The **version badge** opens the Updates page and shows how many updates are ready, the **cog** opens the config page and the **menu** holds the rest.

The menu shows this machine's node name and has **Toggle dark mode**, **Show render HUD**, **Keyboard shortcuts**, **Restart daemon** and **Update assist**. Restart and update both ask before acting.

sections.heading: The daemon
sections.markdown:
Sessions belong to a background daemon, not the web server or the browser tab. Closing the tab or restarting the web server leaves every session running with its scrollback, and any number of browser tabs can watch the same sessions. The web server starts the daemon when it isn't already running, and the daemon exits by itself once it has no sessions and no client has connected for 60 seconds.

- `assist daemon status` shows whether the daemon is running, its live sessions, its links to other machines and any stray daemon processes.
- `assist daemon restart` restarts it. Claude sessions are resumed with `claude --resume` and their scrollback starts fresh; run sessions come back as not-restored cards you can retry. A session the restart interrupted mid-turn is told so when it resumes.
- `assist daemon stop` stops it. Running Claude sessions resume the next time it starts.
- `assist daemon drain` removes every session for a clean slate. It lists the live sessions and asks first (`--yes` skips the question), and a session holding unpushed work is stopped rather than removed.
- `assist daemon run` runs the daemon in the foreground, which is useful when debugging it.

The daemon logs to `~/.assist/daemon/daemon.log`.

One daemon holds at most 24 live sessions, and starting another past that is refused. A restart also brings back at most that many. Change the ceiling with:

```bash
assist config set sessions.maxLive 32 -g
```
